newsitem.title: UK: Daimler says changing hedging technique.
newsitem.headline: Daimler says changing hedging technique.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG said on Thursday that it would change its currency hedging procedures as a result of a negative experience with the sharp depreciation in the value of the mark against currencies like the dollar and pound this year.

"In an effort to avoid these strong, currency-induced fluctuations in future financial results, we will allocate hedging contracts directly to the underlying businesses, despite the high organisational expense this involves," chief financial operating officer Manfred Gentz told reporters.
"With this approach the operating profit will no longer be affected by the market rates, but by the actual hedging rates," he added.

He said earlier that the company's operating result would have been 400-500 million marks better in the first half of 1997 if it had undertaken no hedging at all. But the effect of the weaker mark on profit was a boost of around 300-500 million marks.

"It is difficult to compare the figures exactly as the latter is a theoretical figure. The effect on profit of currencies is not completely neutral but quite neutral," he said, adding that turnover had been boosted by around one billion marks in the first half as a result of the weaker mark.
